full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 21.03.2005 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.101 of 1992 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 17.09.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court, at Khulna in Title Appeal No.120 of 1986 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 31.03.1986 passed by the Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Dacope Upazilla, Khulna decreeing the suit. 

 2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the plaintiff instituted the above mentioned suit being Title Suit No.259 of 1985 in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Dacope, District-Khulna for declaration that enlistment of the suit land as vested and non-resident property and the purported lease of the said land are illegal, malafide and void stating, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands as described in the schedule of the plaint by successive devolution devolved upon one Monindra Bachhar. He died in 1963 in Bangladesh without any issue and wife. After his death, the plaintiff got the suit land as his cousin and since then has been possessing the same. On 15.08.1981, when the employees of local Tahshil Office threatened to dispossess him, he came to know about creation of lease in respect of the suit land as vested and non-resident property. There was no valid reason to declare the suit land as vested and non-resident property. Hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement and denied the material allegations made in the plaint. The case of the defendant is that Monindra left for India before 1965 and consequently the suit land became vested and non-resident property and the Government has been managing the same and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. On conclusion of the trial, the trial Court, considering the evidences and documents on record, decreed the suit by the judgment dated 31.03.1986. 

 5. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.120 of 1986 before the learned District Judge, Khulna. On transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Sub Judge (now Joint District Judge), Commercial Court, Khulna who by the judgment and decree dated 17.09.1999 allowed the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit. 

 6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 17.09.1999 passed by the learned Sub Judge (now Joint District Judge), Commercial Court, Khulna, the plaintiff as petitioner preferred Civil Revision No.101 of 1992 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. 

 7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the par-ties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 21.03.2005 and thereby set aside the judgment and decree dated 17.09.1999 passed by the learned Sub Judge (now Joint District Judge) Commercial Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No.120 of 1986 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 31.03.1986 passed by the learned Munsif now Assistant Judge), Dacope Upazilla, Khulna in Title Suit No.259 of 1985. 

 8. The defendants as petitioners herein feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 21.03.2005 of the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1721 of 2005 before this Division and obtained leave, which, gave rise to the instant appeal. 

 9. Md. Jahangir Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the plaintiff prayed for only relief in Title Suit No.259 of 1985 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dakope, District-Khulna that is for declaration that the enlistment of the suit land as vested and non-resident properties is illegal, void, and without jurisdiction and did not seek any declaration of title, as a result the suit was not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 and, as such, the High Court Division and the Courts below ought to have dismissed the suit on the ground of maintainability but the High Court Division failed to do so and hence, there has been miscarriage of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. 

 12. Leave was granted to examine the following submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General for the appellants-defendants as to that the plaintiff prayed for only relief in Title Suit No. 259 of 1985 of the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dakope, District Khulna that is for declaration that the enlistment of the suit land as vested and non-resident properties is illegal, void, and without jurisdiction and did not seek any declaration of title, as a result the suit was not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and as such the High Court Division and the courts below ought to have dismissed the suit on the ground of maintainability ground but the High Division failed to do so and hence there has been miscarriage of justice. 

 16. It is admitted that the Manindra Bachhar's name was rightly recorded in the SA and RS Ithatians of the suit land. Consequently, the question as to whether the suit was maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 as the plaintiff prayed only for declaration of the enlistment of the suit land as vested and non-resident properties is illegal, void, and devoid of jurisdiction without seeking any declaration of title over the suit land, depends on whether the plaintiff is in possession over the suit land or not. 

 17. P.W. 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 corroborated with P.W. 1 as to that P.W. 1 got the suit land as heir of Manindra Bachhar and possessing the same since his death. Government side was not able to extract contradiction with their statements concerning possession. 

 18. On the other hand, though the Government did not assert in their pleading that they possesses the suit land through anyone, nevertheless, D.W. 2 claimed that he possesses the suit land by leasing out from government and D.W. 3 affirmed D.W. 2's possession. However, D.W. 2 failed to submit any such lease deed and no proper witness appeared to prove his DCR's regarding the suit land. As such, we concur with the findings of the learned Munsif that it is the plaintiff not the defendants possess the suit land. 

 19. The following conditions are to be satisfied for seeking declaratory relieves under Section 42 of Specific Relief Act, 1877 are (1) the plaintiff must be entitled-to a legal character at the time of; the suit, or (2) to a right to property (3) defendant should have denied these or be interested in denying this character or right, and (4) the plaintiff should not be in a position to ask for relief consequential upon declaration sought. On perusal of the plaint it is found that in the present case the plaintiff side fulfills all the first 03 conditions. Side by side, as the suit land's inclusion in the list of Enemy Properties, at present, Vested Properties is illegal; Manindra Bachhar died in this land leaving behind the plaintiffs predecessor as sole heir prior to enforcement of Enemy Properties laws (The Defence of Pakistan Ordinance 1965 and The Defence of Pakistan Rules of 1965) and the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, then it is not a sine qua non to include consequential relief such as declaration of title for getting decree in the instant suit as it's plaint was framed. 

 20. It materializes that the High Court Division, on scrupulous appreciation and sifting of the evidence, both oral and documentary adduced by the plaintiff and defendants and also the other facts and circumstances on record found that the plaintiff's case that they are the owner of the suit property by way of inheritance from Manindra Bachhar, has been proved sufficiently. Appellate Court below erred in both factual and legal aspects of the suit in dismissing the suit. 

 23. Accordingly, this Civil Appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.
